 LIVE UPDATES NFL NFL Week 8 Live Fantasy Football Start 'Em Sit 'Em Lineup Advice and Latest Injury Updates
 Gary Davenport Nov 1, 2026, updated 10 min ago 
 Intermission is over, kids. The second half of the 2026 fantasy football campaign has begun. And that means very different things for different fantasy managers.
 The 6-1 and 5-2 clubs are on riding mowers shaking off bye weeks and injuries because Jaxon Smith-Njigba (my goodness). The 4-3 and 3-4 gang is push-mowing and wishing they had JSN, but they're still in the mix. Past that it's unkempt yards, because it's November and their fantasy team is 2-5 and nothing matters anymore.
 That last paragraph may have emanated from a "discussion" in my house whether the grass needed mowed. I, um, the grass got mowed. And my teams are…sigh.
 Terrible metaphors aside, we're still only halfway to the playoffs. Teams that are rolling are an injury and a couple bad decisions from a skid. Make a waiver claim or two, catch a break and cellar-dwellers can get right back in it.
 No matter the circumstances, if it's victory you seek you've found the right spot, as we'll be updating injuries and offering lineup advice right up until go-time.
 Week 8 Inactives 
 WR A.J. Brown, New England Patriots (knee)
 WR Emeka Egbuka, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (hamstring)
 RB R.J. Harvey, Denver Broncos (knee)
 RB TreVeyon Henderson, New England Patriots (illness)
 RB Kyle Monangai, Chicago Bears (toe)
 WR Rashid Shaheed, Seattle Seahawks (knee)
 WR DeVonta Smith, Philadelphia Eagles (hamstring)
 WR Carnell Tate, Tennessee Titans (shoulder)
 Live Updates
 10 Total Posts
 Newest First ​ 13 mins ago 08:25 AM Sleeper Alert
 AP Photo/Mike Stewart 
 Between injuries, bye weeks and guys who just aren't getting it done (you know who you are), more than a few fantasy managers could use a spot starter at tight end.
 Coming off his bye week, ESPN's Eric Moody believes that Brenton Strange of the Jacksonville Jaguars could be "that guy" in Week 8.
 "Strange might have slipped through the cracks while Jacksonville was on bye last week," he said. "He has had at least seven targets and at least 13 fantasy points in two of his past three games. Now, he faces a Colts defense that has allowed five touchdowns to tight ends this season. For fantasy managers looking to replace George Kittle or Isaiah Likely during their byes, Strange is worth a look."
 25 mins ago 08:13 AM Bills WR D.J. Moore Expected to Play
 D.J. Moore's first season as the No. 1 wide receiver hasn't gone according to plan, but the 29-year-old is expected to return from his shoulder injury Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens.
 The Ravens are allowing the eighth-most PPR points per game to receivers this year, so Moore's on the WR2 radar.
 39 mins ago 07:59 AM Bust Alert
 AP Photo/Melissa Tamez 
 The Chicago Bears are cooking with gas offensively, and quarterback Caleb Williams has been on a roll--he's averaging over 20 fantasy points per start this season.
 Per SI's Michael Fabiano , Williams faces an uphill climb in Week 8 against Seattle's "Dark Side" defense.
 "Williams is a tough player to sit," he said, "but he has a brutal matchup against the Seahawks. Their defense has allowed just one quarterback to beat them for more than 9.8 fantasy points at home, and that includes holding Drake Maye and Patrick Mahomes to fewer than 10 points. Overall, Seattle has allowed the second-fewest fantasy points per game and the second-fewest points per dropback to enemy field generals." 
 49 mins ago 07:49 AM Jaguars WR Jakobi Meyers Expected to Play
 Whew. We really dodged a bullet.
 For a second there, it looked like Brian Thomas Jr. might actually be fantasy-relevant.
 52 mins ago 07:46 AM Roaming the Hall
 It has been over a month since New York Jets running back Breece Hall took the field. And apparently it's going to be at least one more week before the fifth-year veteran returns from his quad injury.
 Braelon Allen is a RB2 (again) in Week 8 against the Raiders.
 1 hour ago 07:38 AM What Can Brown Do for You?
 AP Photo/Nick Wass 
 It has been an underwhelming first half of the fantasy regular season for Cincinnati Bengals running back Chase Brown.
 But Rotoworld's Kyle Dvorchak expects Brown to shake off that sluggish start Sunday against the Tennessee Titans.
 "Brown is currently the league leader in fantasy points under expected among running backs," he said. "Is that a good thing? Of course not. Should we expect it to hold true for the rest of time? No. Entering Week 7, the lowest expected fantasy point totals belonged to Ashton Jeanty, Tony Pollard, J.K. Dobbins, and Quinshon Judkins. Three of them finished as RB1s, and Dobbins found the end zone as well. Volume predicts fantasy production better than anything else and Brown is seeing plenty of it. He's the RB14 in expected points per game. Facing a Titans defense that just got mangled by the aforementioned Judkins, I'm betting on Brown getting back on track this week."
 Brown's a low-end fantasy RB1 this week.
 1 hour ago 07:25 AM I'm Ozzy Osbourne
 Don't ask me, I don't know.
 Fantasy managers with Colts running back Jonathan Taylor probably don't have much recourse but to start him.
 But there's a real chance he's getting dealt, and that could mean fewer touches in Week 8--or even a late scratch.
 The latter might be a blessing. At least the decision would be made for us.
 1 hour ago 07:16 AM We're Not All Sleeping
 I'm forever vigilant for y'all.
 I might be sleeping on the inside, though.
 1 hour ago 07:13 AM Eagles RB Saquon Barkley Not Getting Dealt
 Because fantasy managers didn't already have enough problems, let's add "potential healthy scratch ahead of a trade" to the list.
 Cue Jonathan Taylor managers mumbling as they rock back and forth.
 A Saquon Barkley deal was never especially likely, but it's officially off the table per reports.
 His injuries, on the other hand, are still very much there.
 1 hour ago 07:07 AM WR George Pickens, Jaylen Waddle Expected to Play in Week 8
 There are no shortage of fantasy managers staring at holes in the lineup in Week 8.
 But after popping up on Friday's injury report with a hamstring issue, Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens isn't expected to add to that list--he'll reportedly be a go Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals.
 So will Jaylen Waddle of the Denver Broncos--after getting dinged up on a reverse last week against those same Cardinals a week ago, Waddle is expected to play Sunday afternoon against the Kansas City Chiefs.
